subject: Unexpected increase in billed tokens — request for credit adjustment
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@clearsky.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: billing@clearsky.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected spike and duplicate token charges in June invoice

Hi Laura,

Hope you’re well. We just received the June invoice and noticed a large unexpected increase in billed tokens compared to our usage dashboards — roughly 2.1x what we expected for several daytime windows on 2026-06-29. Attached is our highlighted invoice and a small export of request IDs that look duplicated (see attached: clearsky_invoice_Jun2026.pdf).

Can you confirm whether there were any platform incidents on your side in late June that could have caused double-counting of tokens? If this is on Redwood, we’ll need a retrospective and a credit for the overcharged amount. We’re happy to share the export if it helps with reconciliation.

Thanks,
Jamie Liu
Head of Platform, Clearsky AI
jamie.liu@clearsky.ai

Subject: Re: Unexpected spike and duplicate token charges in June invoice

Hi Jamie — thanks for flagging this and for sending the export. I’m looping in Hannah (CS) and Marcus/Rishi from billing/finance to investigate immediately.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- Marcus will run a token recount and correlate with the request IDs you sent.
- We’ll check incident logs and serving metrics for 2026-06-29 and share any relevant incident/rollback notes.
- If this is a Redwood billing error, we’ll propose a credit and apply it as a deduction on your next invoice (or issue a one-time credit memo if you prefer).

Can you confirm whether you prefer the credit applied to next month’s invoice or a standalone credit memo? Also, if you can share a CSV of the request IDs (full list), that will speed matching.

I’ll update within 48 hours with findings. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Unexpected spike and duplicate token charges in June invoice — urgent reconciliation

Team — forwarding Clearsky’s note and their invoice export. Priority: high.

Initial ask: can we do an end-to-end recount of billed tokens for their account (CLSK-2025-09) for 2026-06-28 to 2026-06-30 and match to provided request_ids? If there was double-counting, we need:
1) root cause summary (incident window + causal mechanism)
2) per-day token delta and $ amount to credit
3) proposed remedy (credit memo + timeline)

I’ve started a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-472 — please add logs/queries there. Marcus, assigning to you as billing owner; Rishi if we need to route financial approval. Hannah — please keep Clearsky in the loop on cadence.

Thanks,
Laura
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Unexpected spike and duplicate token charges in June invoice — urgent reconciliation

Quick update from billing side after an initial pass:

Findings (preliminary):
- We observed an internal replay of KV-prefix caching writes during a runtime rollout on 2026-06-29 between 02:10 and 20:45 UTC. The replay caused a subset of requests to be processed twice by the accounting path, inflating counted tokens.
- Affected traffic window: ~18.5 hours; estimated impacted requests: 38K; estimated duplicated tokens: ~3.1M tokens.
- Estimated gross over-charge: $5,760 (calculated using Clearsky's plan rate and Redwood recorded billing multiplier).

Attachments: I uploaded a spreadsheet with the per-day token deltas and a proposed credit calculation (redwood_credit_adjustment_plan.xlsx) to the ticket. The calculation includes conservative rounding and a 5% buffer for matching uncertainty.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm match against Clearsky’s request_id export (Jamie — please share the CSV).
2) Issue a credit memo for $5,760 to be applied to your July invoice, or issue a one-time credit memo if you prefer immediate refund/offset.
3) Publish a short postmortem description of the bug and the mitigation steps in the Jira ticket (internal).

I’ll prep the credit memo draft once Jamie confirms CSV match. Rishi — can you confirm we are cleared to issue the credit as proposed?

— Marcus
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@clearsky.ai>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike and duplicate token charges in June invoice — proposed credit and timeline

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the CSV you shared. Marcus’s team matched the request IDs and confirmed the duplication.

Summary for Clearsky AI:
- Cause: internal KV-cache replay during a runtime rollout on 2026-06-29 that caused certain requests to be accounted twice.
- Impact window: 2026-06-29 02:10 UTC through 2026-06-29 20:45 UTC.
- Calculated overcharged amount: $5,760.

Proposal: we will issue a credit memo for $5,760 and apply it to your July invoice. If you prefer a standalone credit memo and earlier posting, we can do that immediately instead. The credit memo draft is attached for review (redwood_credit_adjustment_plan.xlsx contains the calculation).

Please reply and confirm which option you prefer (apply to July invoice vs standalone credit memo). Once you confirm we’ll post the credit and send the official memo.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re also publishing an internal postmortem and have put a rollback guard on the rollout path that introduced the bug to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
